# Offering lifecycle FAQ

Synthetic data for tests. Not real.

## 1. Who approves a new offering?

The offering review board approves every new offering. It meets every second Tuesday.

## 2. How long does governance review take?

Governance review takes 10 business days from a complete submission.

## 3. What counts as a complete submission?

A complete submission has a brief with every section filled in, a named owner, and a target GA date.

## 4. Where do I find the offering inventory?

The offering inventory is the shared sheet called Offering Inventory. The owner of each row keeps it current.

## 5. What is the awareness date?

The awareness date is the day the offering team first told the review board about the offering.

## 6. How is time to market measured?

Time to market is the number of days from the awareness date to GA. Offerings without an awareness date are left out.

## 7. Who can change a target GA date?

Only the offering owner can change a target GA date, and the change must be noted in the decision log.

## 8. When is the quarterly offering review?

The quarterly offering review happens in the third week of the last month of each quarter.

## 9. What happens if a brief is incomplete?

An incomplete brief is returned to the owner with a list of the missing sections. Review starts again when it is complete.

## 10. Can an offering skip governance?

No. Every offering goes through governance, including renewals of existing offerings.

## 11. Who do I ask about pricing?

Pricing questions go to the finance partner named in the brief.

## 12. How do I retire an offering?

Send a retirement request to the review board with the last sale date and the support end date.
